evidence: Cato Agr. 151: aquam in āreās (Lewis & Short)
Cic. ND 2.130: Aegyptum Nīlus irrigat (Lewis & Short)

phrases.english: Hold the hose; let’s water the flowers.

phrases.latin: fīgat humō plantās et amīcōs inriget imbrēs
phrases.english: let him set the plants in the ground and water them with kindly showers

phrases.latin: cum sitiunt herbae et pecorī jam grātior umbra est
phrases.english: when the grass is thirsty and the shade is now more welcome to the flock

phrases.latin: sī quidem est eōrum gemmāre vītis, sitīre agrōs, laetās esse segetēs, luxuriōsa frūmenta
phrases.english: since it is their way of speaking (the country people’s) to say that the vines are budding, the fields are thirsty, the crops are happy, the corn is lush

sources: Lewis & Short: rigo · Lewis & Short: adaquo
